verdicts.one_liner: Quotes accurate: description says 'tuple of the matrix element (A,B,C,D)' while docstring/return_line say 2x2 array 'matrix'; a 4-tuple vs (2,2) target broadcast-crashes np.allclose, so the instructed reading hard-fails all tests. Major stands.

All numeric claims verified: np.arccos(1.5+0j)=-0.9624j (so 'keep real part pi' gives pi-0.9624j, opposite sign of target), arccosh(|0.5+1j|)=0.4812118 matches test-1 target imag, cos(pi+0.4812j)=-1.118 != 0.5+1j (target violates the defining equation), complex>1 raises TypeError; steptest re-run: gold-guess recipe PASSES 3/3, plain arccos FAILS test 0. Major stands.

summary: Both findings confirmed (2 confirmed, 0 refuted, 0 uncertain): 39.1 has a genuine tuple-vs-2x2-array return contradiction whose instructed reading crashes the tests, and 39.2 targets are reproducible only via the unstated theta = pi + 1j*arccosh(|trace/2|) recipe that even contradicts the background's cos(theta)=(A+D)/2 on test 1. Both are fixable to fair via the proposed prompt/docstring edits.
